info.title: Breaker API
info.description:
Use the Breaker API to manage campaigns, read your reporting, build segments and work with contacts from your own code. This is the public part of Breaker. Routes that the Breaker app uses internally are not part of this API and are not supported. ## Authentication Every request needs an API key, sent as a bearer token: ```bash curl https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/campaigns \ -H "Authorization: Bearer bk_live_your_key_here" ``` A key belongs to one newsletter. That is why no endpoint takes a newsletter ID. The key already says which newsletter you are working with. To work with more than one newsletter, create a key for each. Owners and admins create keys in the Breaker app under **Settings → API Keys**. The key is shown once, when you create it. Breaker stores only a hash of it, so a lost key cannot be recovered. Create a new key and revoke the old one. Treat a key like a password. Keep it on your server. Never put it in a browser, a mobile app, or a public repository. If a key leaks, revoke it in the app. Revocation takes effect straight away. ## Getting started Five calls that cover most integrations. **1. Create a draft campaign.** ```bash curl -X POST https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/campaigns \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BREAKER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"title": "Weekly roundup", "subject": "Your week in review"}' ``` The draft is created empty. This API cannot send campaigns. A person sends them from the Breaker app. **2. Write its body.** ```bash curl -X PUT https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/campaigns/4821/content \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BREAKER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"html": "

This week

"}' ``` Send an HTML fragment with the styles written into the elements. The endpoint below explains the rules. **3. List what you have.** ```bash curl "https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/campaigns?status=sent&pageSize=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BREAKER_KEY" ``` **4. Read a report.** ```bash curl "https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/reports/summary?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BREAKER_KEY" ``` **5. Find who clicked a link.** ```bash curl https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/campaigns/4821/links \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BREAKER_KEY" curl https://api.breaker.email/v1/public/campaigns/4821/links/97/clicks \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BREAKER_KEY" ``` ## Using Breaker from an AI tool Breaker publishes an MCP server, [`@breaker-email/mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@breaker-email/mcp), so Claude, Cursor, Codex and other AI tools can use this API in conversation. It covers the same endpoints documented here, runs on your own machine, and talks to Breaker with your API key. Nothing is sent anywhere except to Breaker. Create a key in Breaker at [app.breaker.email](https://app.breaker.email) under **Settings** then **API Keys**, then set the server up in your tool: - **Claude Code** — `claude mcp add breaker --scope user --env BREAKER_API_KEY=$BREAKER_KEY -- npx -y @breaker-email/mcp` - **Codex** — `codex mcp add breaker --env BREAKER_API_KEY=$BREAKER_KEY -- npx -y @breaker-email/mcp` - **Cursor** — add the config below to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` - **Claude Desktop** — **Settings**, **Developer**, **Edit Config**, then add the config below - **VS Code** — add the config below to your MCP config, under `servers` rather than `mcpServers` ```json { "mcpServers": { "breaker": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@breaker-email/mcp"], "env": { "BREAKER_API_KEY": "bk_live_your_key_here" } } } } ``` The [package page on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@breaker-email/mcp) carries the same steps in more detail, along with a prompt you can paste into an AI assistant to have it do the setup for you. Web clients that connect to a URL rather than launching a program, such as claude.ai, use Breaker's hosted endpoint instead: ```text https://api.breaker.email/mcp ``` Add it as a remote MCP server or connector and sign in with your Breaker account when the client asks. No API key is involved. The sign-in picks one newsletter, and the connection can be removed in the app under **Settings**, **Integrations**, **AI Clients**. Four things are deliberately not offered as tools, so an assistant cannot do them. Sending a campaign, which stays a decision a person makes in the app. Deleting a campaign or an automation, which cannot be undone. Creating a custom field, whose type is fixed at creation with no way to remove it afterwards. Switching an automation on is not in the API at all, for the same reason as sending. Everything else in this reference is available. Asking for a campaign to be drafted creates a draft and writes its body, leaving it for you to review and send. The same 60 requests a minute apply, shared with any other use of that key.

get.summary: The newsletter this key belongs to
get.description:
The newsletter your API key is scoped to, with its ID and name. A key
belongs to one newsletter, so this tells you which one you are working
in without naming it yourself.

post.description:
Creates an empty draft campaign on your newsletter and returns it.

The draft has no content. Write it with
`PUT /campaigns/{campaignId}/content`, or open the returned `id` in the
Breaker app. A draft created this way is identical to one created with
the **New campaign** button.

Sending is not part of this API. A person sends from the app.

get.description:
Lists campaigns on your newsletter, newest first. Omit `status` to get
every campaign regardless of status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only campaigns with this status. Omit for all.

get.description: Returns one campaign, including its HTML body and email settings.

patch.description:
Updates the campaign's name, subject line or preview text. Send only
the fields you want to change.

This does not change campaign content. Use
`PUT /campaigns/{campaignId}/content` for the body.

delete.description:
Deletes a campaign. **Drafts only.**

A campaign in any other status returns `invalid_request`: deleting a
sent campaign would destroy its reporting history, and this API cannot
send campaigns, so it has no business deleting sends.

400.description: The campaign is not a draft.

error.message: Only draft campaigns can be deleted

get.description:
Returns the campaign as a complete HTML email, wrapped in the sending
template with your newsletter's branding. This is close to what a
subscriber receives, without per-recipient personalisation applied.

Returns the stored body, in exactly the shape `PUT` accepts back. An
empty string means nothing has been written yet.

This is the body on its own. `GET /campaigns/{campaignId}/html` returns
the finished email, with the document wrapper, footer and unsubscribe
block added. That version cannot be written back.

put.description: Replaces the campaign's body with the HTML you send. Send a fragment, not a whole document. Breaker adds the `` and ``, the preview text, your newsletter's footer and the unsubscribe link when the campaign sends. Write your styles into the elements, using `style` attributes. get.description:
Every automation on the newsletter, newest first, on or off. Bodies are
not included; use `GET /automations/{automationId}` for one.

post.description:
Creates an automation with no body, switched off. Write the body with
`PUT /automations/{automationId}/content`, then a person turns it on in
the app.

`audience` decides who receives it. `signupForm` needs the form's
`signupFormId`, from `GET /signup-forms`; every other audience refuses
one. A newsletter holds one automation per audience, and one per signup
form, so a second on the same audience is refused with the id of the
existing one.

everyone.summary: A welcome email for every new contact

value.name: Welcome
value.subject: Welcome aboard
value.previewText: Here is what to expect from us

201.description: The automation, with an empty body.

400.description: A field is invalid, the form is unknown, or the audience is taken.

error.message: Automation 12 already covers this audience. Update it, or delete it first

get.description:
Returns one automation's settings. The body is not included; read it
with `GET /automations/{automationId}/content`.

patch.description:
Changes the name, subject line, preview text, audience or signup form.
Send only the fields you want to change. Moving the audience off
`signupForm` drops the form; moving it onto `signupForm` needs a
`signupFormId` in the same request. The one-per-audience rule applies
to the new audience.

`active` cannot be set here. Switching an automation on is done by a
person in the app. The body is written with
`PUT /automations/{automationId}/content`.

moveToForm.summary: Tie it to one signup form

delete.description:
Deletes an automation, on or off, and drops any contacts still queued
for it. There is no undo.

get.description:
Returns the stored body, in exactly the shape `PUT` accepts back. An
empty string means nothing has been written yet, and an automation with
nothing written never sends, even when it is on.

put.description:
Replaces the automation's body with the HTML you send. The rules, the
`mode` field and the block markup the editor recognises are exactly
those of `PUT /campaigns/{campaignId}/content`; read that operation
for the full reference.

Unlike a campaign, an automation can be written at any time, on or
off: the next contact to arrive receives the new body. Automations
built in Breaker's earlier editor are refused.

value.html:
Welcome

Hi {{contact-first-name|there}}, thanks for joining. Here is what to expect.

get.description:
Returns the body as the send worker renders it, in the content table
with your tracking parameters applied. An automation with no body
returns `invalid_request`.

get.summary: Aggregated stats over a date range
get.description:
Totals across every campaign sent in the window, a per-day series, and
the same totals for the preceding window of equal length so you can
show a comparison.
The same shape as the summary report, narrowed to a single campaign.

One row per contact, with the times they opened, clicked, unsubscribed
or complained. A `null` means the contact did not do that thing.

Every link in the campaign with its click counts. `realClicks` excludes
clicks attributed to security scanners, which is usually the number you
want to report.

The contacts who clicked one specific link, and when. Use this to build
an audience from what people were interested in.
How many contacts are currently subscribed to your newsletter.
How many contacts unsubscribed in the window, with a per-day series.
Every segment on your newsletter, static and rule-driven.

post.description:
Creates a segment, either from a fixed list of contacts or from rules.

**Static** (`type: "static"`, the default): identify contacts by
`contactIds`, by `emails`, or both. Addresses that do not match a
contact on your newsletter are skipped rather than failing the request,
and the response reports how many were matched.

**Dynamic** (`type: "dynamic"`): supply `rules` instead of contacts.
Membership is computed straight away from every subscribed contact, so
the `contactCount` in the response is the segment's real size. The
rule format is described under `SegmentRuleSet`. Every tag, custom
field, campaign, link and signup form a rule names must belong to your
newsletter, or the request fails with `invalid_request` naming the ID
that does not.

A dynamic segment can be opened and edited in the Breaker app like any
other, and its rules can be replaced later with
`PUT /segments/{segmentId}/rules`.

byEmail.summary: Static, from a list of addresses

dynamicAnd.summary: Dynamic, plain AND: one all group
dynamicAnd.description:
Opened at least 2 campaigns in the last 30 days and carries
tag 12. Both conditions must hold, so they sit in one `all`
group.

dynamicOr.summary: Dynamic, plain OR: one any group
dynamicOr.description:
Signed up through form 9502 or ever clicked a pricing link.
Either is enough, so they sit in one `any` group.

dynamicMixed.summary: Dynamic, A and (B or C): two groups
dynamicMixed.description:
In Germany and opened something this month, and either
tagged 12 or clicked campaign 4821. The `all` group holds
the must-haves, the `any` group holds the alternatives, and
the top-level `match: all` requires both groups.

dynamicWinBack.description:
Subscribed before 1 June 2026 and opened nothing in the last
90 days. There is no "not" on a group, so absence is an
`activity` count of exactly 0.

dynamicCustomField.description:
Custom field 44 (from `GET /fields`, a text field) contains
"pro" and the lifetime open rate is 20% or more.

201.description:
The created segment. A static segment also reports what the
contacts you supplied resolved to; a dynamic one is the plain
segment, with `contactCount` set to what its rules matched.

get.description: One segment with its settings and current contact count.

The rules defining a dynamic segment, in the same format
`POST /segments` and `PUT /segments/{segmentId}/rules` accept, so a
segment can be read, adjusted and written back. Static segments return
`null`.

A segment built in the Breaker app may use a condition this API does
not express. Such a condition comes back as `type: "unsupported"` with
the stored node in `raw`, and it is kept as-is if you write the rules
back with the unsupported condition included.

200.description: The rules, or null for a static segment.

put.description:
Replaces the rules of a dynamic segment and recalculates its
membership straight away. The response is the segment with the
`contactCount` the new rules produce.

The whole rule set is replaced, not merged: read the current rules
first if you want to change one condition. Static segments return
`invalid_request`, since their membership is a fixed list.

recentSubscribers.summary: Subscribed this year and never unsubscribed

keepUnsupported.summary: Tighten a segment built in the app, keeping what the API cannot express
keepUnsupported.description:
Read with `GET /segments/{segmentId}/rules`, an extra
condition added, written back. The `unsupported` node came
from the read and is passed through unchanged.

get.description:
The contacts currently in the segment. For a dynamic segment this is
the membership as of the last recalculation.

post.summary: Add contacts to a static segment
post.description:
Adds contacts to a static segment, by ID or email. Contacts already in
the segment are left alone, so this is safe to call repeatedly with
overlapping lists.

Dynamic segments return `invalid_request`: their membership comes from
their rules, not from a list.

Re-runs a dynamic segment's rules and refreshes its membership. Static
segments return `invalid_request`, since there is nothing to
recalculate.

200.description:
The segment after recalculation. `contactCount` is the membership
the rules now produce.

post.description:
Adds a contact to your newsletter.

Custom fields are addressed by their key, which you can list with
`GET /fields`. Unknown keys return `invalid_request` rather than being
silently dropped, and so do tag IDs that belong to another newsletter:
a request is either applied in full or refused.

get.description:
Contacts on your newsletter, newest first.

Filter by `email` to look up the ID for an address you already know,
which is how most integrations start.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Exact address match. Returns at most one contact.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only contacts with this status.

parameters.name: tagId
parameters.description: Return only contacts carrying this tag.

get.description: One contact with its fields and tags.

patch.description:
Updates standard fields, custom fields, or both. Send only what you
want to change. Fields you leave out are not touched.

All changes in one request are applied together. If any field fails
validation, none of them are written.

post.description:
Adds a tag to a contact. Adding a tag the contact already has succeeds
and changes nothing.

delete.summary: Remove a tag from a contact
delete.description:
Removes a tag. Removing a tag the contact does not have succeeds and
changes nothing.

get.description: Whether the contact is subscribed, and when that last changed.

How this contact has engaged across campaigns: what they were sent,
what they opened, and which links they clicked.
Every tag on your newsletter. You need these IDs to tag a contact.

post.description: Creates a tag. Names must be unique on a newsletter.

get.description:
The custom fields defined on your newsletter, with the key you use to
set them on a contact.

post.description:
Defines a new custom field. The `type` fixes what values the field
accepts and cannot be changed afterwards.

get.description:
The signup forms on your newsletter, as built under **Growth** in the
Breaker app. You need a form's `id` for a `signupForm` segment rule,
which matches contacts by the form they subscribed through.

bearerAuth.description:
An API key created in the Breaker app under **Settings → API Keys**,
sent as `Authorization: Bearer bk_live_...`. Each key is scoped to a
single newsletter.

LinkId.name: linkId
LinkId.description: Link ID, from the campaign's links report.

From.name: from
From.description: First day of the window, inclusive, UTC.

To.name: to
To.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, UTC.

XRateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

XRateLimitReset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the window resets.

Newsletter.description:
The newsletter an API key belongs to. Identity only: enough to tell two
keys apart, and to name what you are working in.

CampaignStatus.description: The delivery state of a campaign.

totalItems.description: Items matching the query, across all pages.

CreateCampaignRequest.description: Every field is optional. Send `{}` to create a default draft.

title.description: Internal name, shown in the campaigns list. Not visible to subscribers.

subject.description: Email subject line. Can be left empty and set later.

UpdateCampaignRequest.description: Send only the fields you want to change. At least one is required.

previewText.description: The preview line shown after the subject in most inboxes.

Campaign.description: A campaign, as returned in lists.

id.description: Campaign ID. Use it to open the campaign in the app.

createdAt.description: When the campaign was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

scheduledAt.description:
When the campaign is scheduled to send, or was sent (ISO 8601,
UTC). `null` for a draft.

previewText.description: Preview line shown after the subject.

content.description:
The campaign body as HTML. `null` for a draft with nothing
written yet. This is the body only. Use
`GET /campaigns/{campaignId}/html` for the full rendered email.

html.description: The complete email, wrapped in your sending template.

The stored body, in the same form that `PUT` accepts. Empty when
nothing has been written yet. If the body was sent with
`mode: preserve`, this includes the wrapper element that Breaker
puts around your markup.

The campaign body, as an HTML fragment. Maximum 5 MB.

Breaker adds `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>` when the
campaign sends, so sending them here is refused. `<script>` elements
and inline event handlers such as `onclick` are refused as well.
Everything else is stored exactly as you sent it.

mode.description:
What the Breaker editor should do with this HTML when someone opens
the campaign.

`adopt` stores the HTML as you wrote it. The editor reads it into
its own blocks, so the campaign stays editable in the normal way.
Headings, paragraphs, images and links all become real editor
content. Markup the editor does not recognise is changed or dropped,
and opening the campaign can save that changed version back over
what you sent. Use this when a person will finish the draft in
Breaker.

`preserve` keeps your markup exactly as it is, inside a single HTML
block. It reaches the inbox unchanged. In the editor it shows up as
one block that can only be edited as raw HTML, and editing it there
applies Breaker's list of allowed tags. Use this for templates
designed outside Breaker.

AutomationAudience.description:
Who receives the automation. `all` is every new contact. `imported` is
contacts added by import or by hand. `prospecting` is the prospecting
drip. `signupForm` is one signup form, named by `signupFormId`.
`zapier` is contacts created through Zapier.

Automation.description: An automation's settings. The body is served by the content route.

name.description: Internal name. Subscribers never see it.

previewText.description: Preview line shown after the subject.

signupFormId.description: The form, for a `signupForm` audience. `null` otherwise.

active.description:
Whether new contacts receive it. Read-only: a person switches it
on or off in the app.

html.description:
The stored body, in the same form that `PUT` accepts. Empty when
nothing has been written yet.
The body as the send worker renders it.

name.description: Internal name. Subscribers never see it.

previewText.description: The preview line shown after the subject in most inboxes.

signupFormId.description:
Required for the `signupForm` audience, from `GET /signup-forms`.
Refused for every other audience.

UpdateAutomationRequest.description: Send only the fields you want to change. At least one is required.

signupFormId.description:
Only with the `signupForm` audience, in the same request or already
set. Refused for every other audience.

ReportTotals.description: Counts for a window. Every field is a whole number.

recipients.description:
Contacts the campaigns in scope were sent to, counted over the whole
life of those campaigns rather than only this window. On a campaign
report that is the campaign's own send size. On the summary it is
every campaign in the newsletter. Every other figure here is limited
to the window, so use `delivered` when you want a like-for-like
comparison.

delivered.description: Emails accepted by the receiving server.

realClicksTotal.description:
Clicks with automated scanner traffic removed. Only counted for
campaigns sent after this feature shipped, so historical windows
may report 0 here while `clicksTotal` is non-zero.

ReportSummary.description:
Totals for the window you asked for, the same totals for the preceding
window of equal length, and a day-by-day series.

previousPeriod.description:
The window of the same length immediately before yours, for
comparison. For 1 to 31 August, this is 1 to 31 July.

daily.description: One entry per day in the window, including days with no activity.

Interaction.description:
One contact's engagement with a campaign. A `null` timestamp means the
contact did not do that thing.

id.description: Use this with the link clicks endpoint.

realClicksTotal.description: Scanner traffic removed. See the note on report totals.

type.description:
`static` is a fixed list of contacts. `dynamic` is defined by rules
and recalculated.

matchedContacts.description:
How many of the contacts you supplied were found on your
newsletter and are now in the segment.

unmatchedEmails.description:
Addresses that did not match a contact and were skipped. Empty
when everything matched.

SegmentRules.description: The rules of a dynamic segment, or `null` for a static one.

SegmentRuleSet.description:
What a contact must satisfy to be in a dynamic segment.

A rule set is groups of conditions. Within a group, `match: all` means
every condition must hold and `match: any` means at least one must.
The groups are then combined the same way by the rule set's own
`match`. So "in Germany and opened something this month, and either
tagged VIP or clicked campaign 4821" is one `all` rule set holding an
`all` group and an `any` group.

Only subscribed contacts are considered: a contact who unsubscribes
leaves the segment at the next recalculation whatever the rules say.

Up to 10 groups of up to 15 conditions each. Every condition names its
kind in `type`; the kinds and what each needs are listed under
`SegmentCondition`.

Common recipes, each as one condition:

- Opened at least 2 campaigns in the last 30 days:
  `{"type":"activity","activity":"opened","days":30,"operator":"greaterOrEqual","count":2}`
- Opened nothing in the last 90 days:
  `{"type":"activity","activity":"opened","days":90,"operator":"equals","count":0}`
- Never opened any campaign:
  `{"type":"metric","metric":"uniqueOpens","operator":"equals","value":0}`
- Open rate of 20% or more:
  `{"type":"metric","metric":"openRate","operator":"greaterOrEqual","value":20}`
- Clicked at least once, scanner clicks excluded:
  `{"type":"metric","metric":"uniqueRealClicks","operator":"greaterOrEqual","value":1}`
- Subscribed since 1 January 2026:
  `{"type":"date","event":"createdAt","operator":"onOrAfter","value":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`
- Carries tag 12:
  `{"type":"tag","tagId":12,"operator":"has"}`
- Signed up through form 9502:
  `{"type":"signupForm","formId":9502,"operator":"signedUp"}`
- Clicked campaign 4821:
  `{"type":"campaign","campaignId":4821,"action":"clicked"}`
- Ever clicked a link to your pricing page:
  `{"type":"linkClicked","operator":"contains","value":"/pricing"}`
- In Germany:
  `{"type":"attribute","attribute":"country","operator":"is","value":"DE"}`
- Custom field 44 contains "pro":
  `{"type":"customField","fieldId":44,"operator":"contains","value":"pro"}`

There is no "not" on a group. To exclude, use the negative operator
of the condition: `doesNotHave`, `didNotSignUp`, `isNot`,
`doesNotExist`, or an `activity` count of 0.

RuleMatch.description: `all` means every item must hold; `any` means at least one must.

SegmentCondition.description:
One test on a contact. The `type` says which kind, and each kind has
its own fields:

- `attribute` — a built-in contact or company field, such as
  `country` or `companyName`.
- `customField` — one of your custom fields, by the `id` from
  `GET /fields`. The operators that apply depend on the field's type.
- `tag` — whether the contact carries a tag, by the `id` from
  `GET /tags`.
- `signupForm` — whether the contact subscribed through a signup
  form, by the `id` from `GET /signup-forms`.
- `campaign` — whether the contact was sent, opened or clicked a
  campaign, by the `id` from `GET /campaigns`; or clicked one
  specific link in it, by the `id` from `GET /campaigns/{campaignId}/links`.
- `linkClicked` — whether the contact ever clicked a link whose URL
  matches, across every campaign.
- `date` — when something happened to the contact: created, updated,
  unsubscribed, last opened, last clicked.
- `metric` — the contact's lifetime totals and rates.
- `activity` — how many campaigns the contact was sent, opened or
  clicked in the last N days.
- `unsupported` — only ever returned, never accepted on its own: a
  condition built in the Breaker app that this API does not express.
  Write it back unchanged to keep it.

TextOperator.description:
Operators on text. `exists` and `doesNotExist` test whether the value
is set at all and take no `value`; the rest compare against `value`.

NumberOperator.description:
Operators on numbers. `exists` and `doesNotExist` test whether the
value is set at all and take no `value`.

ComparisonOperator.description: Operators on a number that is always present, such as a total.

DateOperator.description:
Operators on a date. `exists` and `doesNotExist` test whether the event
has happened at all and take no `value`.

BooleanOperator.description: Operators on a true/false custom field. None takes a `value`.

ContactAttribute.description:
The built-in fields of a contact. All are text and take `TextOperator`,
except `companyEmployeeCount` and `companyEstimatedRevenue`, which are
numbers and take `NumberOperator`, and `emailProvider`, which takes
`is`, `isNot`, `exists` or `doesNotExist` with a value from
`EmailProvider`.

EmailProvider.description: The mail provider Breaker detected behind a contact's address.

AttributeCondition.description: A test on a built-in contact or company field.

operator.description: A `TextOperator`, or a `NumberOperator` for the two numeric attributes.

value.description:
Text for text attributes, a number for the numeric ones, an
`EmailProvider` for `emailProvider`. Omit for `exists` and
`doesNotExist`.

CustomFieldCondition.description:
A test on one of your custom fields. Which operators apply follows the
field's type from `GET /fields`: `text` and `url` take `TextOperator`,
`number` takes `NumberOperator`, `boolean` takes `BooleanOperator`, and
`date` takes `DateOperator` with an ISO 8601 `value`.

value.description:
Text for text and url fields, a number for number fields, an ISO
8601 date-time for date fields. Omit for boolean fields and for
`exists` and `doesNotExist`.

TagCondition.description: Whether the contact carries a tag.

SignupFormCondition.description: Whether the contact subscribed through a signup form.

CampaignCondition.description:
Whether the contact was sent, opened or clicked one campaign, or
clicked one specific link in it. `linkId` is required for
`clickedLink` and must be a link of that campaign; it is not accepted
with any other action.

LinkClickedCondition.description:
Whether the contact ever clicked a link whose URL matches, in any
campaign. `exists` means "clicked any link at all" and takes no
`value`; `doesNotExist` is not offered, since every contact who
clicked nothing would match nothing useful.

value.description: The URL, or part of it. Omit for `exists`.

DateCondition.description: When something happened to the contact.

event.description:
`createdAt` and `updatedAt` are the contact record; the other three
are when the contact last unsubscribed, opened and clicked.

MetricCondition.description:
The contact's lifetime engagement. Totals are counts of campaigns;
rates are percentages from 0 to 100, opens or clicks over campaigns
delivered. A contact with no history counts as 0.

The RealClick™ metrics (`totalRealClicks`, `uniqueRealClicks`,
`realClickRate`, `uniqueRealClickRate`) leave out automated inbox
scanner clicks, but only for clicks made on or after 21 August 2026;
earlier clicks count as real. Their rates divide by campaigns
delivered like every other rate: `realClickRate` uses total
RealClicks™, `uniqueRealClickRate` unique RealClicks™.

ActivityCondition.description:
How many campaigns the contact was sent, opened or clicked in the last
`days` days. "Opened at least twice in the last 30 days" is
`activity: opened`, `days: 30`, `operator: greaterOrEqual`, `count: 2`.

UnsupportedCondition.description:
A condition built in the Breaker app that this API does not express.
Returned as-is so nothing is hidden; include it unchanged when writing
the rules back to keep it, or leave it out to drop it. It cannot be
built from scratch here.

raw.description: The stored condition, in the segment builder's own format.

A static segment takes `contactIds`, `emails`, or both, and at least
one contact must match. A dynamic segment takes `rules` and neither
contacts nor addresses.

rules.description: Dynamic segments only, and required for them.

customFields.description: Custom field values, keyed by field key.
Values keyed by custom field key. Unknown keys are rejected.

key.description:
Use this key when setting the field on a contact. It is derived from
the name: lowercased, with every run of non-alphanumeric characters
replaced by an underscore, so "Job Title" is `job_title`. Renaming a
field in the app therefore changes its key, while the `id` does not
change. Read the key from here rather than deriving it yourself.

name.description: The form's title as set in the Breaker app.

tags.name: Automations
tags.description:
One triggered email per audience. An automation goes to every new contact
who arrives through its audience: everyone, imports and manual adds, the
prospecting drip, one signup form, or Zapier. A signup-form automation
wins over the everyone automation for contacts from that form.

Through this API you can draft an automation, write its body in the same
HTML the campaign endpoints accept, and change its settings. It starts
off, and stays off until a person turns it on in the app under
**Automation**; `active` is read-only here. A newsletter can hold one
automation per audience, and one per signup form, so a second one on the
same audience is refused with the id of the one that already covers it.

Contacts queue for an active automation the moment they are created and
receive it within about ten minutes, once each. There is no reporting
per automation.

tags.name: Segments
tags.description:
Groups of contacts, either a fixed list or defined by rules. A segment
is the audience a person picks when sending from the Breaker app. This
API builds and reads segments and does not send.

### Building a dynamic segment

1. Look up the IDs the rules will name: `GET /tags`, `GET /fields`,
   `GET /campaigns`, `GET /campaigns/{campaignId}/links` and
   `GET /signup-forms`. Never guess an ID.
2. Call `POST /segments` with `type: "dynamic"` and `rules`. Leave out
   `contactIds` and `emails`.
3. Read `contactCount` in the response. It is the real membership.
   Zero usually means an operator or value is wrong, not that nobody
   matches.

A rule set is two levels deep, and both levels use `match`:

```json
{
  "match": "all",
  "groups": [
    { "match": "all", "conditions": [ ] },
    { "match": "any", "conditions": [ ] }
  ]
}
```

`match: "all"` is AND. `match: "any"` is OR. The top-level `match`
combines the groups, and each group's `match` combines its own
conditions. For plain AND, use one `all` group. For "A and (B or C)",
use `match: "all"` at the top, an `all` group holding A and an `any`
group holding B and C. For "A or B", use one `any` group. The examples
on `POST /segments` show each shape.

Which condition kind to use:

| You want contacts who... | `type` |
| --- | --- |
| opened, clicked or were sent any campaign in the last N days | `activity` |
| opened, clicked or were sent one specific campaign | `campaign` |
| carry or lack a tag | `tag` |
| have a built-in field value, such as country or job title | `attribute` |
| have a custom field value | `customField` |
| subscribed through a specific signup form | `signupForm` |
| subscribed, unsubscribed, last opened or last clicked before or after a date | `date` |
| have a lifetime total or rate, such as open rate | `metric` |
| ever clicked a URL matching a pattern | `linkClicked` |

Every condition names its kind in `type` and carries only the fields
that kind lists under `SegmentCondition`. `exists` and `doesNotExist`
take no `value`. Dates are ISO 8601 with a time zone. Rates are 0 to
100. One-line recipes for each kind are under `SegmentRuleSet`.

### Field reference

What each condition kind takes. Operators in the `value` column that
say "none" mean the condition carries no `value` at all.

| `type` | Fields | Operators | `value` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attribute`, text | `attribute`: any `ContactAttribute` except the three below | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `doesNotContain`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `exists`, `doesNotExist` | string up to 255 chars; none for `exists`, `doesNotExist` |
| `attribute`, number | `attribute`: `companyEmployeeCount`, `companyEstimatedRevenue` | `equals`, `notEquals`, `greaterThan`, `greaterOrEqual`, `lessThan`, `lessOrEqual`, `exists`, `doesNotExist` | number; none for `exists`, `doesNotExist` |
| `attribute`, provider | `attribute`: `emailProvider` | `is`, `isNot`, `exists`, `doesNotExist` | one of `EmailProvider`; none for `exists`, `doesNotExist` |
| `customField`, `text` or `url` field | `fieldId` from `GET /fields` | the text operators above | string up to 1000 chars |
| `customField`, `number` field | `fieldId` | the number operators above | number |
| `customField`, `boolean` field | `fieldId` | `isTrue`, `isFalse`, `exists`, `doesNotExist` | none |
| `customField`, `date` field | `fieldId` | `after`, `onOrAfter`, `before`, `onOrBefore`, `exists`, `doesNotExist` | ISO 8601 date-time; none for `exists`, `doesNotExist` |
| `tag` | `tagId` from `GET /tags` | `has`, `doesNotHave` | none |
| `signupForm` | `formId` from `GET /signup-forms` | `signedUp`, `didNotSignUp` | none |
| `campaign` | `campaignId` from `GET /campaigns`; `linkId` from `GET /campaigns/{campaignId}/links`, only with `clickedLink` | `action`: `sent`, `opened`, `clicked`, `clickedLink` | none |
| `linkClicked` | none | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `doesNotContain`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `exists` | the URL or part of it, up to 1000 chars; none for `exists` |
| `date` | `event`: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `unsubscribedAt`, `lastOpenedAt`, `lastClickedAt` | `after`, `onOrAfter`, `before`, `onOrBefore`, `exists`, `doesNotExist` | ISO 8601 date-time; none for `exists`, `doesNotExist` |
| `metric` | `metric`: `totalSent`, `totalDelivered`, `totalOpens`, `uniqueOpens`, `totalClicks`, `uniqueClicks`, `openRate`, `uniqueOpenRate`, `clickRate`, `uniqueClickRate`, `totalRealClicks`, `uniqueRealClicks`, `realClickRate`, `uniqueRealClickRate` | `equals`, `notEquals`, `greaterThan`, `greaterOrEqual`, `lessThan`, `lessOrEqual` | number, required. Totals are campaign counts. Rates are 0 to 100. RealClick metrics exclude scanner clicks from 21 August 2026 onward |
| `activity` | `activity`: `sent`, `opened`, `clicked`; `days`: 1 to 365 | `equals`, `notEquals`, `greaterThan`, `greaterOrEqual`, `lessThan`, `lessOrEqual`, default `greaterOrEqual` | `count`: how many campaigns in the window, 0 or more |

How values are compared:

- `exists` means the field is filled in. `doesNotExist` means it is
  empty. An empty field never matches `isNot`, `doesNotContain` or
  `notEquals`, so "country is not DE" leaves out contacts with no
  country. Add `doesNotExist` in an `any` group to include them.
- Text comparison ignores case, so `country is de` matches `DE`.
  `contains`, `startsWith` and `endsWith` are substring matches.
- `metric` values are never empty. A contact with no sending history
  counts as 0 on every metric, and a rate is opens or clicks divided by
  campaigns delivered, as a percentage capped at 100. The RealClick™
  metrics (`totalRealClicks`, `uniqueRealClicks`, `realClickRate`,
  `uniqueRealClickRate`) leave out automated scanner clicks, but only
  for clicks made on or after 21 August 2026; earlier clicks count as
  real. Their rates use the same delivered denominator.
- `activity` counts campaigns whose event falls in the last `days`
  days, measured from now at recalculation time. `count: 0` with
  `equals` means "none in the window".
- `campaign` with `clickedLink` needs `linkId`, and refuses it with any
  other action.
- `linkClicked` with `exists` means "clicked any link in any campaign".
  There is no `doesNotExist`, since it would match nobody.
- A `date` value is compared as an instant, so `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`
  and `2026-01-01T02:00:00+02:00` are the same moment.
